title: Raymond Scott's quintet, Mitch Miller and Alec Wilder
summary: Hinton and Leeman recall Raymond Scott's famous quintet and big band with Mitch Miller and Lou Shoobe, and the quintet playing the Jack Benny Show theme.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: He was a great player -- some of them used to be jazz players at one time.
Well, you had Mitch Miller - remember the great band that Raymond Scott had with Mitch Miller playing oboe, and ...
That was Mark -- that was Mark's band, his brother, before me. Because I ended up -- I finished a Hit Parade, I was just getting to that.

I'm talking about the band that made all of those things like 'A Little Girl Grows Up' and all of these beautiful records which I have now, which were Raymond Scott's records. And Lou Shoobe was a bass player.
He used to have a quintet.
Yeah.
Oh, that was a big thing.
But that was Mark Warner's? It wasn't Raymond Scott's?
No, that was Raymond's band -- Raymond Scott and his quintet.
Yeah, that's exactly what I'm saying.
Oh, I misunderstood you. What's his name used to also be in that band.
With Mitch Miller.
Mitch was in the big band, too.

And I'm a black musician, but I remember every facet of music that's interesting to me, and I try to recognize all of it, and I've tried to see it. Raymond Scott, with Lou Shoobe playing bass, with Mitch Miller playing oboe, and with Frank Ara playing bass -- I can recall every member's name in that band.
You're right -- that was just a little bit before me.
That's right, I remember.
And we used to emulate some of those songs.
And those records are fantastic. They were using Alec Wilder's music.
Right.
He was one of our truly American composers. I'm sorry I interjected that, I just wanted to get to that, because you were of that era.
Well, we had the quintet, we were on every Sunday on the Jack Benny Show, we played the theme song.
Right.
